attributes.title: Level 8

subgroups.name: build 1

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use a base and accent color to design a grass tile asset, like this?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What color might be used as the accent color to add details to the grass tile asset?

❓ How can custom tile assets be created in MakeCode Arcade?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Point out to the ninja that tile assets can be created in the Assets menu. Alternatively, tile assets can be created within the tilemap editor in the My Tiles section. Tile assets in My Tiles can be edited, duplicated, and deleted. Remind the ninja that the size of all tile assets are 16x16, which cannot be changed.
steps.instructions:
Create a tilemap to use in the project! 


Click the Assets menu along the top of the screen, then create a new 16 x 16 tilemap asset. Give the tilemap asset a descriptive name.


On the left side of the tilemap editor, select My Tiles then create a new tile by clicking +. Design a grass tile that uses green as a base color, then select another color to add subtle accents to the tile. Give the tile asset a descriptive name.


Click Done, then fill the tilemap with grass tiles.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you design and place road tiles on the tilemap so that all of the roads are connected?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What color might be used to create a road tile asset?

❓ Where might road tiles be placed on the tilemap to create a network of roads?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Prompt the ninja to think about what color roads typically are, then select a color that matches in the tile editor.

💡 Encourage the ninja to place road tiles around the entirety of the tilemap. Remind the ninja that all roads should be connected, meaning there should be 1 contiguous path that a sprite can move around when the project is built and run.
steps.instructions:
Design a road tile and create a map of connected and intersecting roads on the tilemap.


Click on My Tiles and + to create a road tile. Keep it simple with just a solid color; corners and crosswalk road tiles will be created in the next few steps. Give the tile asset a descriptive name. 


Place the road tiles on the tilemap to create a network of roads. Leave spaces in between the roads so you can add other tiles, such as trees or buildings, later.

steps.hints: ❓Did you create and place the 4 different curved road tiles in the appropriate road corners on the tilemap?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Why is it necessary to create 4 curved road tile assets?

❓ Where might the curved road tile assets be placed on the tilemap?

❓ How might pixels be connected to create a curved edge in the tile asset?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Because roads are connected in all different directions, it’s important to create 4 different curved road tiles to reflect this. 4 tile assets must be created because if 1 tile asset were to be flipped, it would flip all of the tiles of that type on the tilemap. 

💡 Have the ninja identify the intersection points of each of the road tiles already on the tilemap and replace any corners with the curved road tile asset that match the direction.

💡 Remind the ninja to use the documentation for help when creating a curved line in pixel art. Prompt the ninja to consider how they are connecting pixels, how many pixels are in each “step”, and to use the erase tool to remove any jaggies in the line.
steps.instructions:
Design and place 4 curved road tiles on the tilemap.


Under My Tiles, select the road tile then click to duplicate the tile. Select the new tile, then click to edit it.


Create a curved road tile. In the tile editor, use the erase tool to remove pixels from the top left half of the image. Then, use a lighter outline color to draw a curved line from the top right corner of the canvas, to the bottom left. Connect the pixels diagonally and remove any jaggies. Fill in the outer edge with the same color as the grass tile. Give the tile asset a descriptive name.


Duplicate and rotate the tile to create 3 other tiles that have curved edges in all 4 directions. Place the 4 different curved road tiles on the tilemap wherever there are corners.

steps.hints: ❓Did you place crosswalk tiles on the road where it might make sense, such as before an intersection or a corner?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ How might a crosswalk be added to the road tile asset?

❓ Where might crosswalk tiles be placed on the tilemap?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Prompt the ninja to place the crosswalk tiles in logical places around the tilemap. Brainstorm with them places that they typically see crosswalks in real life (such as at intersections). In the next steps, houses and buildings will be added which can be placed at or near the crosswalk tiles as well.
steps.instructions:
Design and place a crosswalk tile on the tilemap.


Select the road tile then click to duplicate the tile. Select the new tile, then click to edit it. Use white to draw evenly spaced crosswalk lines along the middle of the tile. Give the tile asset a descriptive name.


Replace some road tiles with a crosswalk tile on the tilemap.

steps.hints: ❓Did you create 4 distinct house tiles by switching up the color and/or placement of the windows, doors, or flowers?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What colors and shapes might be used to design a house tile? 

❓ How might you modify the placement of each feature in the original house tile to create 4 unique house tiles?

❓ Where might house tiles be placed on the tilemap?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Encourage the ninja to tinker with different shapes and colors to design their house tile. They may opt to use squares and rectangles to design the door, window, and frame of the house. Remind the ninja to use the pixel art techniques they’ve already learned about, such as dithering, analogous colors, and complementary colors to create and modify their house tile assets.

💡 The ninja should place house tiles around the road tiles on the tilemap. They may opt to place them at or near the crosswalk tiles added in the previous step. Prompt the ninja to consider how many house tiles should be added to the tilemap and how they should be spaced apart.
steps.instructions:
Design and place house tiles on the tilemap.


Create a house tile using squares and rectangles to draw only the main part of the house, including windows and doors. Add sidewalks, flowers, or other elements to the front of the house, too. Do not draw a roof, as this will be designed as a separate tile in the next step. Give the tile asset a descriptive name. 


Duplicate the tile to create 3 other houses. Change the colors of the house, doors, flowers, or flip the placement of the windows and doors to create different house tiles. 


Replace some grass tiles with the 4 different house tiles on the tilemap.

steps.hints: ❓Did you use complementary colors on the 2 halves of the roof to show the contrast between the side that gets more light and the side that gets less light?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ How might pixels be connected to create a triangle shaped roof tile?

❓ What colors might be used in each roof tile asset?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja to use the documentation for help when creating diagonal lines in pixel art. Prompt the ninja to consider how they are connecting pixels, how many pixels are in each “step”, and to use the erase tool to remove any jaggies in the line.

💡 Prompt the ninja to consider what 2 colors should be used to create contrast in the roof tile. Have the ninja use the documentation to identify complementary colors that can be used to show a brighter and a darker side of the roof.
steps.instructions:
Design and place roof tiles on the tilemap.


Create a roof tile using diagonal lines to form a triangle shaped roof.  Use complementary colors to fill in the sides of the roof, using a brighter color on the side that gets more light, and a darker color on the side that gets less.


Fill the empty space above the roof with the grass tile color so there will not be empty spaces on the tilemap. Give the tile asset a descriptive name. 


Duplicate the tile to create another roof style. Change the colors of the roof to make them look different. 


Add roof tiles on top of the house tiles on the tilemap.

steps.hints: ❓Did you use complementary colors to show contrast in the house addition tiles?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What other tile designs might be created to add onto the existing house tiles? 

❓ What other features are typically found on or near a house?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Prompt the ninja to brainstorm other features that a house might have (such as a garage, a unique roof, specific plants, etc.). Encourage the ninja to tinker with the shapes and colors needed to create this feature in pixel art. Have the ninja use base colors already found in the house tiles to connect multiple tiles together. Then, have the ninja place the house addition tiles in the appropriate places on the tilemap.
steps.instructions:
Design and place house addition tiles that can be combined with the house tiles on the tilemap.


Create new tiles that can be combined with the house tiles to make the house larger than a single tile. Consider creating tiles that have a garage, a second floor, or another type of house addition!


Place the new house addition tiles on the tilemap to create larger houses!

steps.hints: ❓Did you create a variety of building tiles, then place them together to create other places on the tilemap?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What other buildings might you find in a city?

❓ How might different designs be connected to create a multi-tile building?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Prompt the ninja to brainstorm other buildings that might be found in a city (such as a school, store, museum, Code Ninjas location, etc.). Encourage the ninja to tinker with the shapes and colors needed to create this feature in pixel art. 

💡 Have the ninja think through what type of building they want to create first, then think more specifically about the types of features that might be found in that building. For example, a store front might have a small door with a large street window or a school building might have large doors with multiple floors. Encourage the ninja to tinker with the placement of each tile on the tilemap, then update each asset as needed to make sure they fit together well.
steps.instructions:
Design and place several other building tiles that can be put together to create a larger multi-tile building on the tilemap.


Create several building tiles that can be put together to create a larger building in the city such as a school, museum, or store. Create the tiles in the same theme colors so they fit together like a puzzle.


Use rectangles, diagonal lines, highlights and shadows to create different building elements that can be combined in a variety of ways. Consider creating an entryway door tile, a wall with windows tile, and different types of roof tiles.


Place the new building tiles on the tilemap to create more buildings!

steps.hints: ❓Did you use complementary colors to add dithering to the leaves, and other colors to create highlights and shadows for the tree?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What colors might be used to design a tree tile asset? 

❓ How might you use dithering to add depth to the tree tile?

❓ Where might tree tiles be placed on the tilemap?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja to use the pixel art techniques they’ve already learned about, such as dithering, highlights, and shadows to design their tree tile asset.

💡 Prompt the ninja to consider where tree tiles might be placed on the tilemap (such as near houses and buildings, in empty tilemap space, near a crosswalk, etc.).
steps.instructions:
Design and place tree tiles on the tilemap.


Create a tree tile. Start by coloring the background the same green as the grass tile. Draw the trunk and branch with 2 darker colors such as brown and purple. Use another shade of green to add in the leaves, and add in some dithering to give the tree some depth. Add a shadow on the bottom of the tree with another dark color to add contrast. 


The entire tree should fit on the tile. Give the tile asset a descriptive name. 


Replace some grass tiles with a tree tile on the tilemap.

steps.hints: ❓Did you use the fill tool to add walls to large sections of tiles that are are not road or crosswalk tiles?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Which tiles should not have walls turned on?

❓ What tool(s) can be used to add walls to the tiles on the tilemap?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that they can use the show walls toggle to turn the wall display on and off in the tilemap editor.

💡 Remind the ninja that they can select both the fill and draw walls tools to add walls to a large section of tiles on the tilemap. The erase and draw walls tools can be used together to remove any accidental walls.



💡 Point out to the ninja that because tile assets are 16x16 squares, portions of the curved road tile assets act as walls, even though they appear to be grass.
steps.instructions:
Turn walls on and display the tilemap.


Add walls to all of the tiles that are not road or crosswalk tiles! Use the fill tool to set large sections of walls.


Return to the JavaScript editor, then add the tilemap to the project.


Click ▶ to see the tilemap on the screen.

steps.hints: ❓Did you use placeOnRandomTile to set the Player sprite to appear on a random road tile?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Where should the Player sprite be placed on the tilemap?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja to use the documentation for help with any of the Player sprite’s functions.
steps.instructions:
Add a moveable Player sprite to the project.


Notice the sprite image assets already in the Assets menu. Create a Player sprite using the bikeRight asset. Place the sprite on a random road tile. Code the sprite to move with direction buttons and set the camera to follow the sprite. 


Click ▶ to test the Player sprite’s code.

steps.hints: ❓Did you use the Show Previous Frame tool to compare the different frames?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Where might highlights and spokes be placed in each of the frames of the bikeRightAnim animation asset?

❓ Do the bike’s wheels appear to be turning in the Animation preview window? 


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Encourage the ninja to tinker with the placement of the highlights and spokes in each frame of the animation asset, to make it appear as if the bikes wheels are turning. Prompt the ninja to test the animation in the preview window, then tinker with the image frames to make it more realistic.

💡 Remind the ninja that the Show Previous Frame tool can be found in the lower left corner of the animation paint editor, and can be used for comparing the position of an image in the previous frame, with the current frame.
steps.instructions:
Create the Player sprite’s biking right animation using multiple frames!


In the Assets menu, select the bikeRight asset and click Copy under the Asset Preview pane. Create a bikeRightAnim animation asset, then paste the image into the first frame in the animation paint editor. 


Duplicate the frame to create a total of 4 frames, adjusting the wheel highlights and spokes in a clockwise rotation to show the progression of movement in each frame.


Preview the animation on the upper right part of the screen, then make any adjustments to refine the animation.

steps.hints: ❓Did you use the Show Previous Frame tool to compare the different frames?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Where might highlights be placed in each of the frames of the bikeUpAnim animation asset?

❓ Do the bike’s wheels appear to be turning in the Animation preview window? 


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Encourage the ninja to tinker with the placement of the highlights in each frame of the animation asset, to make it appear as if the bikes wheels are turning. Prompt the ninja to test the animation in the preview window, then tinker with the image frames to make it more realistic.


💡 Remind the ninja that the Show Previous Frame tool can be found in the lower left corner of the animation paint editor, and can be used for comparing the position of an image in the previous frame, with the current frame.
steps.instructions:
Create the Player sprite’s biking up animation using multiple frames!


In the Assets menu, select the bikeUp asset and click Copy under the Asset Preview pane. Create a bikeUpAnim animation asset, then paste the image into the first frame in the animation paint editor. 


Duplicate the frame to create a total of 4 frames that use highlights that move progressively lower on the wheel to show the progression of movement in each frame.


Preview the animation on the upper right part of the screen, then make any adjustments to refine the animation.

steps.hints: ❓Did you preview the animation on the upper right part of the screen to ensure each frame was flipped correctly?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What tools can be used to flip the direction of the frames in an animation asset?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that they can use the horizontal and vertical flip tools, found in the top left corner of the animation editor, to change the direction of frames in an animation asset.
steps.instructions:
Create the biking left and biking down animation assets!


Duplicate the bikeRightAnim animation asset, then rename the new asset bikeLeftAnim. Use the horizontal flip tool to flip the image in each frame to create left facing sprite images.


Repeat this process with the bikeUpAnim animation asset to create a bikeDownAnim animation asset.

steps.hints: ❓Did you add on button pressed events for right, left,  up, and down buttons so that the sprite animation updates to the correct direction?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What should happen when each direction is pressed? 


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 When each direction button is pressed, the matching animation asset should show on screen, so that the Player sprite’s image appears to be moving in that direction. Prompt the ninja to test out the project to make sure the correct  animation assets appear as expected.
steps.instructions:
Match the Player sprite’s animation to the direction that it is biking. 


Return to the JavaScript editor and code the Player sprite’s animation to change on button pressed events. Update the runImageAnimation parameters accordingly.


Click ▶ to test the sprite animation when the direction buttons are pressed.

steps.hints: ❓Did you update the walls on any tiles that were changed on the tilemap design?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What other tiles might be added to customize the tilemap’s design?

❓ What else could be added to turn this into a full project? 


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Encourage the ninja to brainstorm other objects that might be found in a city, that are not currently present on the tilemap’s design. The ninja can create new custom tiles, then place them strategically on the tilemap. 

💡 In this activity, the ninja focused only on creating the assets for the project. Prompt the ninja to consider what else could be added to turn this project into an engaging game for the user.
steps.instructions:
Explore the city tilemap!


Move the Player sprite in different directions and notice how the different tiles have been combined to create a city world. Create additional tiles, such as flowers, shrubs, or rocks, to decorate the grass area. Adjust the tilemap design as needed to improve the layout.


Click ▶ to explore different parts of the city tilemap.

subgroups.title: We Built this City!
subgroups.introduction: Create different custom tile assets to build a tilemap of a city!

validationItems.text: Design a top-down tilemap using at least 10 original grass, road, building, and tree tiles.
Create and use animations to show the Player sprite biking in all 4 directions.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 8 of Brown Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about creating original tile assets to build unique tilemaps. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 8:

badges.title: Mapping It Out
badges.description: Use a variety of pixel art techniques to create original tile assets that can be used for top-down or 2D tilemaps.

badges.title: A Whole New World
badges.description: Create original tile assets, including ground terrain and floating platform tiles, that can be used to design a 2D tilemap.

badges.title: Open Concept
badges.description: Create original tile assets that can be combined in a variety of ways to design structures that span multiple tiles.

badges.title: Changing It Up
badges.description: Change a sprite’s movement ability based on its location in relation to a specific tile kind.
